newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Motoinvest in talks on Sporitelna stake.
newsitem.headline: Motoinvest in talks on Sporitelna stake.

text.p: The Czech investment group Motoinvest said on Wednesday that it was in talks to sell its shares in the largest Czech savings bank Ceska Sporitelna to a foreign investor, but declined to say how large the stake is.
"Domestic offers aren't so attractive," Motoinvest general director Pavel Tykac told a news conference in Prague.
He declined to say how big Motoinvest's holding in Sporitelna was, but said his colleague Libor Sadilek was abroad representing Motoinvest in talks to sell the shares.
Any transfer of banking shares to a foreign investor must be approved by the Czech National Bank.

Motoinvest, under central bank review for its involvement in the fall of Kreditni Banka a.s. and links to Agrobanka a.s. which was put under forced administration on Tuesday, held a stake of about 10 percent listed at Sporitelna's general meeting in May.

Tykac, who left the country Monday saying he feared for his safety after levelling allegations of loan kickbacks against a deputy of a prominent political party, returned on Wednesday to say Motoinvest was looking to divest all its banking holdings.
Motoinvest is a secretive investment group which was involved in takeover battles for several Czech privatisation funds last autumn.
One representative of Motoinvest, David Knop-Kostka, is under indictment on fraud charges for a debt swap scheme he allegedly help engineer at the now-defunct Kreditni Banka.
